## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
`Cache.set` needs a fix before merge because it stores keys without lower-casing them, so `get` cannot find any entry written with a mixed-case key.

## Changes
The pull request adds a `Cache.set` method and raises `DEFAULT_TTL` from 60 to 300 seconds, updating the comment to match. It also adds tests for the set/get round trip, the default TTL value and expiry.

## Critical
- app/cache.py:27 — correctness — Lower-case the key in Cache.set — `c.set("ALPHA", 1)` followed by `c.get("ALPHA")` returns `None`: `set` stores under `"ALPHA"`, but `get` looks up `key.lower()` (line 17). This breaks the rule at app/cache.py:14-15: "every path into _store lower-cases the key first". `test_set_then_get_round_trip` passes only because it sets lowercase `"alpha"`. — Callers who use mixed-case keys get cache misses on every read, and their entries stay in `_store` because `get` never reaches them to evict them. — Fix: store under `key.lower()`, and extend `test_set_then_get_round_trip` to set a mixed-case key.
